C001.reason: Required reference: encoding must use speedKph with mps converted to kph via *3.6 before encoding. TypeScript bindings use camelCase speedKph for the renamed field.

C002.reason: Required reference: observation key becomes speed_kph and field name is speedKph; value must be decoded float32 exposed as JSON number. Need to convert entity speedKph from kph to display.

C003.reason: Required reference: threshold changes to >108.0 kph (was >30.0 mps); uses entity.speedKph field. Need to update constant and field reference.

edits.before: const sample = VehicleTelemetry.encode({ vehicleId: request.vehicle_id, speedMps: request.speed }).finish();
edits.after: const sample = VehicleTelemetry.encode({ vehicleId: request.vehicle_id, speedKph: request.speed * 3.6 }).finish();

edits.before: const fields = { vehicle_id: entity.vehicleId, speed_mps: entity.speedMps };
edits.after: const fields = { vehicle_id: entity.vehicleId, speed_kph: entity.speedKph };

edits.before: return { fields, speeding: entity.speedMps > 30.0, constructed_payload: Buffer.from(sample).toString("base64") };
edits.after: return { fields, speeding: entity.speedKph > 108.0, constructed_payload: Buffer.from(sample).toString("base64") };

rationale: Schema rename from speed_mps to speed_kph with unit conversion at encoding time (mps * 3.6 = kph). Threshold for speeding changes from 30.0 mps to 108.0 kph (same physical speed). Observation key changes from speed_mps to speed_kph. The TypeScript bindings generate speedKph for the protobuf field speed_kph. All three candidates are required references that must be edited to maintain correct behavior through the full request->encode->decode->observe path.
assumptions: TypeScript protobuf bindings use camelCase speedKph matching protobuf snake_case speed_kph
Float32 precision is handled by protobuf library; we expose the decoded value directly
Entity fields use the same naming convention as generated bindings (speedKph not speedMps)
No mixed unit/version handling needed; coordinated rollout only
